settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

candidates.description: SandboxTransformer.interceptConstructor applies only to ConstructorCallExpression nodes that are not special calls (lines 402-414): the code explicitly declines to intercept super(...)/this(...) because bytecode requires them to be the first statement of a constructor. The compensating control is processConstructors (lines 159-232), which rewrites constructors into a private constructor taking a Checker.SuperConstructorWrapper and a public constructor whose first statement routes super arguments through checkedSuperConstructor. Because the mechanism depends on precise AST shapes (body.get(0) being an ExpressionStatement wrapping a ConstructorCallExpression; declaredConstructors heuristics), a construct yielding a body not matching the assumed shape could produce a constructor whose super(...) arguments are never offered to the interceptor. Static reading could not establish a concrete Groovy snippet that evades the rewrite, so this is an open question, not a confirmed bypass.
missing_evidence: No Groovy test snippet demonstrating an evading constructor body shape was constructed or executed
Runtime behaviour showing checkedSuperConstructor is always reached was not verified
No interceptor implementation in this repository demonstrates onSuperConstructor enforcement
preconditions: Host relies on GroovyInterceptor.onNewInstance/onSuperConstructor to authorize object creation of attacker-influenced classes
Untrusted Groovy source compiled with SandboxTransformer (interceptConstructor left at default true)
A Groovy construct produces a constructor body not matching the shape assumed in processConstructors
candidates.title: Constructor interception gap for super(...)/this(...) relies wholly on processConstructors rewriting (SECURITY-582 area)

candidates.description: Checker.checkedCast is the interception point for cast expressions and for implicit coercion of Collection/Map right-hand sides. Inside it, blocks deliberately discard the interceptor's return value (interface candidate methods invoked with default-valued parameters; positional-argument constructors for Collection/Map values; File construction from a CharSequence), existing only to give the interceptor the opportunity to throw. Execution then continues to the genuine conversion. Consequence: a host interceptor that implements policy by transforming/substituting values rather than throwing gets no effect on the cast path — a sanitizing replacement is silently discarded for the interface-method and positional-constructor notifications, and the original value is still coerced. New File(...) is constructed from an attacker-supplied string even though the interceptor saw the would-be call.
missing_evidence: No interceptor in this repository relies on the value-substitution pattern
No test exercises the File-from-CharSequence branch
Whether the real Groovy runtime would invoke the same constructors anyway (making notification additive) was not verified against Groovy 2.4.7 sources
preconditions: Host interceptor filters/modifies values instead of purely throwing
Untrusted script performs a cast/coercion matching one of the branches (interface target; concrete Collection/Map positional constructor; File from CharSequence)
candidates.title: checkedCast notifies interceptors but ignores their decisions before performing the real coercion

candidates.description: In SandboxTransformer.innerTransform, an assignment whose left-hand side is a FieldExpression falls through to super.transform with an in-source comment noting the static/field access cannot be intercepted and is being skipped. Similarly, property assignment to an implicit-this name resolving to an existing field of the visited class returns a raw BinaryExpression without checkedSetProperty wrapping. Field access via FieldExpression is thus invisible to GroovyInterceptor, while the equivalent x.@field attribute access is intercepted through checkedGetAttribute/checkedSetAttribute. For a sandbox whose policy is expressed only as interceptor callbacks, any object reachable by the script whose fields are directly referenceable can be read/written without any callback — a divergence between attribute and field paths a policy author might not expect.
missing_evidence: No concrete Groovy snippet compiled to confirm when FieldExpression vs AttributeExpression is produced
No demonstration that a realistic policy is defeated solely via field access
Behaviour under the Groovy 2.4.7 compiler pipeline was not verified
preconditions: Untrusted Groovy source compiled with SandboxTransformer
Script references a field lowered to FieldExpression rather than Attribute/PropertyExpression
Host policy relies exclusively on interceptor callbacks for read/write control
candidates.title: FieldExpression and direct implicit-this field assignment are intentionally left untransformed

candidates.description: The VariableExpression branch in SandboxTransformer.innerTransform is guarded by `exp instanceof VariableExpression && interceptProperty`, and the implicit-this-to-PropertyExpression conversion is only reached through that same flag. Consequently, disabling only interceptProperty (nominally controlling property access) also stops rewriting of non-local variable expressions that map to implicit-this property access, so a bare name resolving to a property/field access would be evaluated by untransformed Groovy dispatch and never offered to the interceptor. This is a configuration-coupling issue, not a demonstrated bypass; it is reported because a host disabling interceptProperty to reduce overhead may lose callbacks it believed were governed by other flags.

Whether Groovy property resolution could still be caught by the fallback invoker chain was not analysed
preconditions: Host sets interceptProperty = false while keeping other flags enabled
Untrusted script uses bare non-local identifiers resolving to implicit-this property access
candidates.title: interceptProperty flag couples property interception with rewriting of non-local variable reads/writes

candidates.description: GroovyInterceptor keeps interceptors in a per-thread CopyOnWriteArrayList and exposes them via an unmodifiable view. register() appends; unregister() removes by equals(). Because removal uses List.remove(Object) semantics, a sandbox that re-registers the same instance or unregisters in a non-LIFO order can silently drop a different interceptor layer than intended, since the list is order-sensitive and each element is consulted in turn. There is no scoped/try-finally registration helper in this repository, so an exception thrown during script evaluation combined with manual unregister() calls can leave the thread's interceptor list unexpected; Checker would then dispatch script calls to a reduced (or empty) chain, in which case each invoker chain's fallback executes the real operation. This is a lifecycle/robustness concern around a security-relevant registry, not a demonstrated bypass.
missing_evidence: No host integration code in this repository to inspect, so such patterns cannot be confirmed
No evidence any interceptor overrides equals() in a way that would make List.remove affect the wrong element
Runtime behaviour of the interceptor chain under exception unwinding was not tested
preconditions: Host registers/unregisters multiple GroovyInterceptor instances on the same thread
Registration/unregistration is not wrapped in try/finally, or the same instance is registered more than once
Evaluation of untrusted script propagates exceptions out of the block performing the unregister
candidates.title: Per-thread interceptor registry lifecycle: non-LIFO unregister with no scoped helper for a security-relevant chain
